text.text_excerpt: If you are in the neighborhood this is a FINE option for groceries, produce, prepared foods and liquor. The prices aren't always the best, so be sure to pay attention. They have a great selection of fresh vegetables and lots of international packaged items. I went specifically looking for ingredients for a central American dish, thought I would find what I needed here (canned roasted peppers) but they didn't have what I needed, they did, however have 17 different varieties of pickled peppers, so there is that! It was very clean, not too crowded, lots of items to choose from, I will definitely stop in from time to time. But, I prefer the Ideal market a few block up Broad for Latin options.

Its a well maintained smallish grocery store. I am impressed with the fresh produce, fruits and vegetables! So nice to see actual stock! Very good selection of meats. Seems to be geared to hispanic and possibly Middle Eastern fare. Cow heart, beef tongue, and of course all the regular stuff. Tortillas are fresh, lot of spices and salsas to choose from. Lot of wines, some beer, good prices on liquor. I like it!

Tuesday I read about @big_easy_freshmarket on @nolanews, and I was in that market by Wednesday to pick up some produce -- papaya & plantain -- and then I was back again today for their tempting-looking hot line. : : Their bakery, beer cave, and neatly stacked produce (trust me, those with acute OCD will love this place's attention to detail) are all impressive, BUT those pans full of freshly prepared food were calling me back. : : They offer your typical fried foods, like fish, chicken, and fries; but they also split up the line between Hispanic food and Middle Eastern cuisine. Today, I went for lamb with white beans over saffron rice, kibbeh, some type of veggies, and some type of wheat ...
